Subject: Private deployment priming: account & network punchlist

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on — we’re excited to get the private deployment rolling with Redwood. Before we schedule the technical screening call, the internal infra team asked me to confirm a short "priming" punchlist so we can ensure our security and networking folks are ready. High-level asks below: 

- Confirm Redwood-managed egress IPs or a recommended approach for stable egress (we prefer explicit ranges we can allow in firewall).
- KMS integration options (bring-your-own-key vs. Redwood-managed) and required service account permissions.
- Audit / telemetry retention expectations and access method (S3/Cloud Logging access, log formats).
- Required ports and protocols (ingress/egress) including any NAT/UDP needs.
- Preferred connectivity: VPN / Direct Connect / PrivateLink (we currently run Direct Connect and can stand up a VPN tunnel).
- Doc/attachment with sample network diagram + example firewall snippet would be super helpful.

We can share internal diagrams once we have the expected egress ranges and whether mutual TLS or client certs are required. Can you draft the minimal checklist items we should validate before the screening call?

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Halcyon Health

Ellen — thanks, this is a perfect starting point. I pulled together a concise priming checklist so your team can validate internal readiness ahead of the screening call. Attaching a short PDF with our standard Minimum Customer Prereqs (MCP-prereqs.pdf). Please confirm the items below: 

Redwood private-deploy priming checklist (minimal):
1) Networking
  - Provide desired connectivity mode: Direct Connect (preferred), VPN, or PrivateLink.
  - Provide CIDR(s) that will accept Redwood egress ranges (we'll provide ranges below).
  - Approved outbound: HTTPS (443) to Redwood control & model endpoints; optional ports listed for metrics/tracing.
2) IP allowlisting
  - Confirm if you can allow a set of stable egress IP ranges. If not, we’ll use mutual TLS + hostname allowlisting as fallback.
3) KMS & keys
  - Decide BYOK (customer KMS) vs Redwood-managed keys. For BYOK: create an encryption key with an admin service principal and provide key ARN + grant.
4) Service accounts & IAM
  - Create a dedicated service account for Redwood infra access with minimal roles (list included in MCP doc).
5) Audit & telemetry
  - Identify where audit logs should be exported (S3 bucket or Cloud Logging project), retention window, and who has access.
6) Ports & egress
  - Confirm port 443 outbound allowed for all runtime hosts. If you plan to use prometheus or metrics pulling, note ports 9090/9100 as optional.
7) Maintenance window
  - Preferred weekly maintenance window for patching/rollouts (TZ + 2-hour slot).

Next steps: Ben will follow up with the concrete egress ranges and a small example firewall snippet and network diagram. Once Halcyon confirms, let’s pick a 60-minute technical screen — I can offer Tue/Wed next week (09/19 or 09/20) 10–11am PT.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: MCP-prereqs.pdf (1 page — checklist + service-account role matrix)

Ellen — adding the concrete network bits from ops that usually unblock infra teams quickly. Attaching a quick network diagram and a tiny firewall snippet.

Key egress & firewall guidance (example):
- Outbound: 443 TCP to model-control.redwood-inference.com (FQDN) and to model-hosting endpoints.
- Recommended allowlist (example ranges): 52.34.128.0/18, 13.59.0.0/16, 3.11.64.0/18
  - NOTE: if your security team does not allow IP ranges, we support mTLS + hostname validation for control plane calls.
- Inbound: None required to Redwood runtime hosts if you use Direct Connect/VPN NAT — all traffic is outbound from your infra to Redwood endpoints.
- NAT/UDP: No special UDP rules required for normal model inference; metrics scrape requires TCP 9100/9090 if you plan to pull metrics.

Example firewall snippet (for your perimeter NAT):
# allow outbound HTTPS to Redwood endpoints
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 FROM 10.5.0.0/16 TO 52.34.128.0/18
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 FROM 10.5.0.0/16 TO 13.59.0.0/16

If you want we can provide CA certs for client-auth and sample iptables rules for an on-prem bastion.

Attachments: network-diagram.png (PNG, 640x480), sample-firewall-snippet.txt

Ben Carter
Private Deploy Operations
ben_carter@redwood.com
